evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

step_0_ratio.note: Not a clean rune/item multiplier (no 1.6, 2.0, 1/0.6 = 1.6667, 1.08, 1.25 candidate matches). It is, to 4 decimals, 1 + R/100 for R = 68.6 -- i.e. exactly the pre-mitigation-to-post-mitigation damage ratio against 68.6 armor.

step_1_overheal_algebra.definition_used: overheal = max(0, heal_landed - missing_health)  (the heal-side analogue of the engine's documented clipping identity for shields: 'absorbed = min(shield, damage), overkill = max(0, damage - absorbed)', docs/math-foundations.md Section 5)
step_1_overheal_algebra.work: Let H = heal amount, M = missing health of the healed unit, r = H_new/H_old. If M is unchanged, (r*H - M)/(H - M) = 148.4/88.0 = r forces M*(r-1) = 0, hence M = 0.
step_1_overheal_algebra.conclusion: The healed unit was at FULL health, the whole heal was wasted, so overheal == heal amount. The heal itself went 88.0 -> 148.4, growing by exactly the factor 1.686.

step_2_identify_the_factor.mitigation_identity: docs/math-foundations.md Sections 2.1 / 5: m(R) = 100/(100+R); EHP round-trip raw = post*(1 + R/100).
step_2_identify_the_factor.work: 1 + R/100 = 1.686364 => R = 68.64 (tolerance from 1-decimal rounding of both leaves: R in [68.49, 68.79]).
step_2_identify_the_factor.why_68_6: No champion in data/champions.json has ~68.6 armor OR ~68.6 magic resistance at level 18 or 20 under the growth formula base + growth*(L-1)*(0.7025 + 0.0175*(L-1)) (scanned all entries; zero hits in [68.3, 68.9] for MR, zero natural hits for armor). 68.6 is a DERIVED resistance: 98 armor x 0.70 = 68.6 exactly -- a 98-armor target under Black Cleaver's full 5-stack Carve, which is the item the scenario is named after.
step_2_identify_the_factor.armor_98_targets: Rell, Shaco, Sivir, Tristana are exactly 98.0 armor at level 18 (base 30, growth 4); Cassiopeia 97.9, Malzahar 97.9, Taliyah 97.9, Twisted Fate 97.95, Viktor 97.8, Nilah 98.4, Lillia 98.5 also round to 98 under the engine's documented integer stat rounding (math-foundations Section 5, 'Stat rounding ... APPROX').
step_2_identify_the_factor.black_cleaver_source: data/items.json 3071 Black Cleaver, passive Carve: 'Dealing physical damage to an enemy champion applies a stack of Carve for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction, up to 30% at 5 stacks.'

independent_computation.step_3_what_the_change_is: The healing event is a damage-linked heal off PHYSICAL damage dealt to the Cleaver-shredded target (armor, not MR, is what Carve reduces). Its basis moved from the POST-mitigation damage (88.0) to the PRE-mitigation / raw damage (148.4). No other mechanism in the cached data produces exactly the 100/(100+R) factor.

step_4_which_basis_is_correct.rule: The cached wiki text words each heal's basis explicitly, and for physical damage-linked healing it is post-mitigation essentially everywhere. Pre-mitigation is the rare, explicitly-worded exception.
post_mitigation_sources_quoted: data/champions.json Aatrox E Umbral Dash: 'Passive: Aatrox heals for 16% (+ 1.1% per 100 bonus health) of non- persistent post-mitigation damage he deals against enemy champions.'
data/champions.json Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance: 'Aatrox heals for the post-mitigation bonus damage dealt, reduced to 25% against minions.'
data/champions.json Kayn R (Rhaast): 'Rhaast heals for 25% (+ 0.5% per 100 bonus health) of the post-mitigation physical damage that he deals to enemy champions with his abilities.'

data/champions.json Ambessa R: 'heals herself for a percentage of the post-mitigation damage she deals'; Camille W: 'healed for 100% of this additional damage post-mitigation'; Viego P, Warwick P/Q/R, Gwen P, Nilah Q/R, Morgana P, Hecarim R, Briar W Snack Attack, Aphelios P: all worded 'post-mitigation'.
data/runes.json Conqueror: 'at which you also heal for 8%/5% of the post-mitigation damage dealt against enemy champions.'

data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json e9-item-bloodthirster-lifesteal: 'Bloodthirster 15% lifesteal: 8 autos of 134.1 post-mitigation damage -> 8 heals of 20.1' (item life steal is post-mitigation in this corpus).
pre_mitigation_exceptions_and_why_they_a: Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ('heals himself for 30% of the pre-mitigation damage dealt') - MAGIC damage; Black Cleaver does not shred magic resistance, and no champion has 68.6 MR at level 18/20, so the observed armor-shaped factor cannot come from it. Also already pinned pre-mitigation by data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json e0-vladimir-sanguine-pool-heal (raw 75.0 -> heal 22.5), i.e. baseline, not a new flip.

Fiddlesticks W ('heals itself for a portion of the pre-mitigation damage dealt') - MAGIC damage; same exclusion. data/champion-audit/batch-1.json also records the W heal as unmodeled ('Fiddlesticks absent from HEALING_RULE_CHAMPIONS').

Briar P Crimson Curse ('The bleed always heals Briar for 25% of the pre-mitigation damage dealt') - the only PHYSICAL pre-mitigation heal in the cache, but ruled out on magnitude: the sourced heal rows are 2.5 : 12.5 (based on level) (+ 12.5% bonus AD) per bleed application over its duration, i.e. at level 18 with 5 stacks at most (12.5 + 0.125*bAD) * 2.0 over 5 s. Reaching a single 148.4 heal event would require ~1,000 bonus AD. It is also already implemented on the pre-mitigation basis at baseline (data/champion-audit/batch-p1-3.json Briar: 'P Crimson Curse now heals 25% of the bleed's pre-mitigation damage per tick').
step_4_which_basis_is_correct.conclusion: Every damage-linked heal that could plausibly fire in this scenario -- item life steal / omnivamp, the Conqueror keystone, and the modelled champion self-heals off physical damage -- is worded 'post-mitigation' in the cached wiki text. Dropping mitigation from the basis overstates the heal by exactly 100/(100+68.6)^-1 = 1.686x.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' does not live under data/, so the healer's identity is inferred, not read: the 1.686 factor is armor-shaped (Black Cleaver shreds armor only), which fixes the heal as a physical damage-linked heal.

The verdict would flip to new_value_correct only if the heal source were one of the three explicitly pre-mitigation-worded heals. All three are excluded above (two are magic damage; Briar's is physical but two orders of magnitude too small for a 148.4 single event, and is already pre-mitigation at baseline).

An alternative reading -- that the underlying physical damage itself stopped being mitigated (double-mitigation fix) rather than the heal basis changing -- produces the identical 1.686 factor. That reading is also wrong for this leaf: the heal is defined on the damage that actually landed, and 100/(100+R) mitigation must be in the basis either way.
